# 1 Clement Chapter 20 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 20 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_020_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 20

**[TRANSLATOR'S NOTE: Chapter 20 is the cosmic hymn of 1 Clement — a meditation on creation's ordered obedience to its Sovereign Lord. Drawing on Stoic cosmological vocabulary, Clement surveys the heavens, the earth, the sea, the seasons, and even the smallest creatures, and finds in each a model of harmonious obedience. The implicit argument: if all creation submits to God's order, how much more should the Corinthians?]**

**20:1** The heavens, moving under his governance, are subject to him in peace. Day and night accomplish the course appointed by him, in no way hindering each other.

**20:2** The sun and the moon and the choir of stars roll on in harmony through their appointed courses according to his ordinance, without any transgressing his command.

**20:3** The earth, bearing fruit in fulfillment of his will at their proper seasons, brings forth food in abundance for men and beasts and all the living creatures that are upon it, not dissenting and not altering any of his decrees.

**20:4** The unsearchable depths of the abyss and the inexpressible regions of the underworld are bound by the same ordinances.

**20:5** The hollow of the boundless sea is brought together by his workmanship into its appointed basins, and does not pass beyond the barriers set around it, but does as he commanded it;

**20:6** For he said: "Thus far shall you come, and your waves shall be broken within you." [Job 38:11]

**20:7** The impassable ocean and the worlds beyond it are regulated by the same commands of the Master.

**20:8** The seasons of spring, summer, autumn, and winter give way to each other in peace.

**20:9** The stations of the winds complete their seasonal course without obstruction. The ever-flowing springs, made for enjoyment and for health, present their life-giving breasts without fail for the sustenance of men.

**20:10** The smallest of living creatures meet together in peace and harmony.

**20:11** All these things the great Craftsman and Master of all willed to exist in peace and concord, bestowing his goodness upon all things, but most abundantly upon us who have fled for refuge to his mercy through our Lord Jesus Christ,

**20:12** to whom be glory and majesty forever and ever. Amen.

---

*LOGOS: "choir of stars" for *chorous* — preserves the cosmic-dance image of Greek cosmological thought.*
